arxiv-2102-05498.title: Dysplasia grading of colorectal polyps through convolutional neural network analysis of whole slide images Thanks: This project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement No 825111, DeepHealth Project.
arxiv-2102-05498.creator: Daniele Perlo 1, Enzo Tartaglione 1, Luca Bertero 2, Paola Cassoni 2, Marco Grangetto 1
arxiv-2102-05498.description: Abstract Colorectal cancer is a leading cause of cancer death for both men and women. For this reason, histo-pathological characterization of colorectal polyps is the major instrument for the pathologist in order to infer the actual risk for cancer and to guide further follow-up.

arxiv-2109-02144.title: Shadows are Bicategorical Traces
arxiv-2109-02144.creator: Kathryn Hess and Nima Rasekh
arxiv-2109-02144.description: Abstract . The theory of shadows is an axiomatic, bicategorical framework that generalizes topological Hochschild homology (THH) and satisfies analogous important properties, such as Morita invariance. Using Berman’s extension of THH \mathrm{THH} to bicategories, we prove that there is an equivalence between functors out of Hochschild homology of a bicategory and shadows on that bicategory.

arxiv-2112-01116.description: Abstract FASER is a new experiment designed to search for new light weakly-interacting long-lived particles (LLPs) and study high-energy neutrino interactions in the very forward region of the LHC collisions at CERN. The experimental apparatus is situated 480 m downstream of the ATLAS interaction-point aligned with the beam collision axis.

The model function f f is unknown and belongs to a Hölder-type smoothness class with parameter β \beta .

arxiv-2601-01498.description: Abstract The advancement of LLM agents with tool-use capabilities requires diverse and complex training corpora. pmc-11471781.creator: Favour Abumere Imohiosen, Edwin Andrew Ofudje, Khairia Mohammed Al-Ahmary, Saedah R. Al-Mhyawi, Ibtehaj F. Alshdoukhi, Mazen R. Alrahili, Ahad Amer Alsaiari, Salah Ud Din
pmc-11471781.description: Pharmaceutical effluents generated during drugs production and application are often times released into the water systems with little or no treatment, which could pose potential danger to the ecosystem. Advanced oxidation processes for organic pollutants treatment have gained wide consideration due to their effectiveness.

pmc-11545561.title: Predictors and Profile of Severe Infectious Complications in Multiple Myeloma Patients Treated with Daratumumab-Based Regimens: A Machine Learning Model for Pneumonia Risk
pmc-11545561.creator: Damian Mikulski, Marcin Kamil Kędzior, Grzegorz Mirocha, Katarzyna Jerzmanowska-Piechota, Żaneta Witas, Łukasz Woźniak, Magdalena Pawlak, Kacper Kościelny, Michał Kośny, Paweł Robak, Aleksandra Gołos, Tadeusz Robak, Wojciech Fendler, Joanna Góra-Tybor
pmc-11545561.description: Simple SummaryOur research explores the profile and risk factors for infections in multiple myeloma patients undergoing treatment with daratumumab, a key drug in chemotherapy regimens for this disease. The study seeks to identify which patients are at the highest risk of developing severe infections and the factors contributing to this risk, as infections are a major concern for these patients.

pmc-11689968.title: RESILIENCE: A “CURE” FOR OR A “RESPONSE” TO AGING?
pmc-11689968.creator: Chao Fang, Alastair Comery, J D Carpentieri
pmc-11689968.description: Resilience is often perceived as an intrinsic ability to adapt to challenges. Grounded in the human psyche, research commonly depicts it as a self-defence mechanism, enabling people to navigate and overcome adversity. Sociological thinking questions this view, suggesting that resilience should not merely involve adaptation but also foster positive change in challenging situations.

pmc-12422812.title: Leg blood flow and cardiac output are cyclically reduced during low‐intensity exercise with intermittent KAATSU cuff inflation in young adults
pmc-12422812.creator: Stuart P S Mladen, Stacey P A Forbes, Abby K Zedic, Patrick J Drouin, Vaughn S England, Michael E Tschakovsky
pmc-12422812.description: The present investigation sought to determine the cardiovascular responses to a commercially available KAATSU cuff system with rhythmic cuff inflation–deflation periods during leg exercise. Seventeen participants performed two‐legged knee flexion/extension exercise at 25% of peak work rate (WRPeak) with bilateral KAATSU cuffs applied to the proximal thigh (KAATSU) or work‐rate matched control exercise (CTL).

pmc-12597293.title: Power of public health advice: Effectiveness and spillover effects of federal vaccine recommendations
pmc-12597293.creator: Junying Zhao, Ahmed El Fatmaoui, Mahla Shourian, Bethanie Lor, Pallab K. Ghosh
pmc-12597293.description: ObjectivesThis paper focuses on the national-level, inexpensive, demand-side vaccine policy—federal recommendations. It evaluates the effectiveness of 2008 and 2010 influenza vaccine recommendations, the spillover effect of the 2009 H1N1 vaccine recommendation on influenza vaccination, and heterogeneous policy effects across individual characteristics.Study designObservational study with before-after comparison assessing changes in vaccination following policy implementation.

pmc-12621150.title: Microbial Protein for Human Consumption: Towards Sustainable Protein Production
pmc-12621150.creator: Anthony W Watson, Rebecca F Townsend, Matt Longshaw
pmc-12621150.description: Protein from animal sources significantly contributes to greenhouse gas emissions, driving the need for sustainable alternative protein sources to meet global dietary demands while reducing environmental impact. This project explores microbial protein, derived through cellular agriculture using fermentation technology, as a viable, sustainable and high‐quality protein for human consumption.

pmc-12788228.title: Essential Tremor Severity Assessment Using Handwriting Analysis and Machine Learning
pmc-12788228.creator: Jose Ignacio Sánchez Méndez, Elsa Fernandez, Alberto Bergareche, Karmele Lopez-de-Ipina
pmc-12788228.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: Essential tremor (ET) is among the most common neurological disorders, requiring precise diagnosis and severity assessment for personalized and effective management. Methods: This study explores an innovative approach to evaluate ET severity using the gold-standard Archimedes spiral test. The family-based dataset covers the entire range of tremor severity, from very mild (level 1) to advanced stages, offering a valuable resource for studying early diagnosis and tracking disease progression.

pmc-12806133.title: The impact of asymmetrical gene expression on the development of spike morphology in Triticum aestivum
pmc-12806133.creator: Fang He, Xiaojuan Liu, Qian Ma, Wei Wan, Luhua Li, Kuiyin Li, Zhenzhen Jia, Suqin Zhang, Ruhong Xu, Mingjian Ren
pmc-12806133.description: Wheat yield is primarily determined by panicle density per unit area, grain count per spike, and grain weight. The proliferation of wheat spikes affects both the number of grains per spike and grain weight. However, the molecular regulatory mechanisms of wheat spike development are still largely elusive.

pmc-13107837.title: Cross-cultural adaptation of the Italian version of the “Child and Youth Mental Health Instrument for Developmental Disabilities” (I-ChYMH-DD)
pmc-13107837.creator: Elisabetta Sforza, Chiara Leoni, Elena De Rosa, Jacopo Bellani, Germana Viscogliosi, Antonella Di Paola, Marta Zampino, Rita Fischetto, Marika Pane, Donato Rigante, Serenella Servidei, Guido Primiano, Roberta Onesimo, Angelo Carfì, Zampino Giuseppe
pmc-13107837.description: BackgroundThe Child and Youth Mental Health and Developmental Disability ChYMH-DD is a psychometrically rigorous tool for care planning for children with developmental disabilities. It allows paediatricians and other healthcare professionals to perform a comprehensive assessment of children functional status and family burden.

pmc-13616812.title: Color-Flow Doppler Detection of Partial Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Drainage in a Dog
pmc-13616812.creator: Abigail T. Kaplan, Kailah M. Buchanan, Weihow Hsue
pmc-13616812.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Graphical abstract

Introduction

Left-to-right shunting at the pulmonary venous level can be categorized as anomalous connection or anomalous drainage.1 Partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection (PAPVC) refers to abnormal linking of some of the pulmonary veins (PVeins) to the right atrium (RA) or its tributaries without normal connection to the left atrium (LA), whereas total anomalous pulmonary venous connection involves all PVeins. In most cases, the terms “anomalous pulmonary venous connection” and “anomalous pulmonary venous return” are used interchangeably.

pmc-13631143.title: Fingolimod Acutely Facilitates the Activation of TRKB in a BDNF-dependent Manner
pmc-13631143.creator: Cecilia Anna Brunello, Paula Pastor Muñoz, José Pedro Araujo, Nina Seiffert, Katja Kaurinkoski, Plinio Casarotto, Caroline Biojone, Eero Castrén
pmc-13631143.description: Fingolimod (FNG) is a sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor agonist currently prescribed for the treatment of remitting-relapsing multiple sclerosis. However, an increasing body of evidence indicates that FNG has a variety of other effects on the central nervous system, making it a good candidate to target other brain disorders that display loss of neuronal cells and synaptic plasticity.

pmc-13643469.title: When the Aorta Speaks
pmc-13643469.creator: Yasuhiro Maejima
pmc-13643469.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Corresponding AuthorKey words: aortic coarctation, computed tomography, echocardiography, vascular disease

Takayasu arteritis (TAK) remains one of the most challenging forms of large-vessel vasculitis because of its heterogeneous clinical presentation, unpredictable disease course, and complex therapeutic decision-making. Although remarkable advances in vascular imaging and immunosuppressive therapy have substantially improved patient outcomes, delayed diagnosis remains common, particularly among patients with atypical clinical characteristics.

pmc-13674298.title: Construction and implantation of a modified trileaflet polytetrafluoroethylene valved conduit for pulmonary valve replacement
pmc-13674298.creator: Abel Getachew, Nikita Zadneulitca, Ashok Muralidaran, Castigliano M Bhamidipati, Yoshio Ootaki
pmc-13674298.description: ObjectivesHandmade expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) valved conduits have emerged as a durable and cost-effective option for pulmonary valve replacement. We have reported excellent results of trileaflet ePTFE valved conduit and the longest follow-up exceeded 10 years. Technical precision during valve construction and implantation is critical to optimize valve function and conduit geometry, and we recently modified the technique.
